data.name: Ramanathan
data.gender_notes: Ramanathan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit words ‘Rama’ and ‘Anath’, meaning ‘Jewel of Rama’. This name is of great significance in Hindu mythology, as Rama is an avatar of the god Vishnu and a central figure in the ancient Indian epic ‘Ramayana’. Ramanathan represents strength, virtue, and devotion. The name Ramanathan carries the meaning “Jewel of Rama” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ramanathan usually hope their child will grow to embody jewel of rama and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes devotion and connection to the divine through the name of Rama, an avatar of Vishnu.
data.etymology: Ramanathan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Jewel of Rama.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ramanathan total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

vedic_reference.note: Ramanathan is a Sanskrit name derived from Rama (God) and Anatha (God of Death). In Hindu mythology, Rama is an incarnation of Vishnu, who is known for his righteousness, strength, and devotion to his wife, Sita. The name Ramanathan can be seen as an expression of the belief that Rama, the god of righteousness, can protect one from the god of death, Anatha.
